title: Adjective Declension 8: Mixed Review
description: Synthesis. All six cases × singular and plural × the husher / velar spelling rule. The four-step diagnostic (gender / number → case → spelling rule → ending) runs the full grid.
descriptionRussian: Повторение: все шесть падежей в единственном и множественном числе плюс орфографическое правило для шипящих и заднеязычных. Диагностический алгоритм: род / число → падеж → орфография → окончание.
intro: The full grid at once. Four steps produce any form: gender and number, then the case from whatever triggered it, then a check on whether a spelling rule fires, then the ending. The triggers are ones you have been collecting since A1, so nothing here is new except having to run all four steps without pausing.
rules: The full hard-stem adjective grid: 12 cells across cases and numbers. Memorise the column patterns: masc-and-neut merge from genitive onward; feminine pins to -ой for four oblique cases; plural collapses gender entirely.
Husher / velar spelling rule (Rule 1): in any ending where the regular form has -ы, write -и after к / г / х / ж / ш / ч / щ. So -ый → -ий, -ые → -ие, -ых → -их, -ым → -им, -ыми → -ими.
Four-step diagnostic to produce a form: gender / number → case (read the trigger) → spelling rule (check the stem) → ending (read off the grid).

Triggers covered across the track: nominative (subject, это, у меня), acc (direct object), gen (нет, без, для, из, у), dat (помогать, звонить, к, age, нравится), instr (с + accompaniment, profession, гордиться, под / за / над / перед), prep (в, на, о / об, при).
examples: Это новая школа. (This is a new school.) Step 1: fem sg. Step 2: nom (это). Step 3: no rule. Step 4: -ая. → новая.
Я знаю старого друга. (I know the old friend.) Step 1: masc sg animate. Step 2: acc (direct object, animate). Step 3: no rule. Step 4: -ого. → старого.
У меня нет хороших друзей. (I don't have good friends.) Step 1: pl. Step 2: gen (нет + gen). Step 3: husher -ш-, so -ых → -их. Step 4: -их. → хороших.
Маша помогает маленьким детям. (Masha helps little children.) Step 1: pl. Step 2: dat (помогать). Step 3: velar -к-, so -ым → -им. Step 4: -им. → маленьким.
Антон работает с русским коллегой. (Anton works with a Russian colleague.) Step 1: masc sg. Step 2: instr (с + accompaniment). Step 3: velar -к-, so -ым → -им. Step 4: -им. → русским.
Лена думает о красивом озере. (Lena thinks about the beautiful lake.) Step 1: neut sg. Step 2: prep (о + topic). Step 3: no rule. Step 4: -ом. → красивом.

items.promptEnglish: Anton is proud of his smart sisters.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 7: гордиться + instr; plural instrumental.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 7. Гордиться + instr. Plural instr ending is -ыми: умными. Today's drill mixes all cases.

items.promptEnglish: I am reading a new book.
items.hint: Step 1: fem sg. Step 2: acc (direct object). Step 4: ending?
items.explanation: Fem sg, acc, no spelling rule. Feminine acc ending is -ую: новую. The -ую appears only in the feminine accusative singular; the other four feminine oblique cases all use -ой.

items.promptEnglish: Masha lives in a big city.
items.hint: Step 1: masc sg. Step 2: prep (в + location). Step 4: ending?
items.explanation: Masc sg, prep, no spelling rule (the ending is stressed -ом, not unstressed; Rule 2 only triggers in unstressed position after a husher). Большом. Note that большой is end-stressed, so the -ом kept its -о.

items.hint: Step 1: pl. Step 2: gen (нет). Step 3: no rule. Step 4: ending?
items.explanation: Pl, gen, no spelling rule. Plural gen ending is -ых: новых. Книг is the gen pl of книга (zero ending after a feminine -а).

items.hint: Step 1: masc sg. Step 2: dat (звонить). Step 4: ending?
items.explanation: Masc sg, dat, no spelling rule. Masculine dat ending is -ому: старому.

items.hint: Step 1: pl. Step 2: dat (помогать). Step 3: velar -к-: rule applies. Step 4: ending?
items.explanation: Pl, dat, velar -к- triggers Rule 1: -ым → -им. Маленьким. Дети is the plural of ребёнок (a completely different word); its dat pl is детям. The same -им appears in русским, хорошим, большим across all four oblique plural cases.

blanks: Антон работает с _____ коллегой. (Anton works with a Russian colleague.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: С + instr triggers the instrumental. Коллега is masculine (despite ending in -а; one of the rare masc -а nouns). Русский ends in the velar -к-, so by Rule 1 the masculine instr is -им: русским.

errorCorrection.explanation: Two steps combine here: учителя are animate, so the plural accusative borrows the genitive ending -ых, and the husher -ш- then swaps -ы to -и by Rule 1, giving хороших. Хорошых is the form Rule 1 forbids and is not valid. This is the four-step diagnostic at work: number, then case, then spelling, then ending.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha often calls her new teacher.
errorCorrection.explanation: Звонить governs the dative, so the masculine adjective takes -ому: новому учителю. Нового is the genitive and animate-accusative form (я знаю нового учителя), an easy mix-up because the stem is the same.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша уже год живёт в новым доме.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha has been living in a new house for a year now.
errorCorrection.explanation: В answering 'where' takes the prepositional, so the masculine adjective takes -ом: новом доме. Новым is the instrumental (с новым домом would need an instrumental trigger like с or под), a frequent slip because -ом and -ым look close. The trigger в + location pins the case as prepositional.

minimalPairs.explanation: Fem sg, acc (direct object). The feminine acc ending is -ую: новую. Новой would mark the genitive, dative, instrumental, or prepositional, all of which would need a different trigger.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Anton is proud of the little children.
minimalPairs.explanation: Гордиться + instr triggers the instrumental, not the genitive. Plural instr after a velar is -ими: маленькими. Маленьких would be the gen pl ('нет маленьких детей').

patternRecognition.question: Why does the adjective end in -ого?
options: Step 1: masc sg, Step 2: gen (acc inanimate)
Step 1: masc sg animate, Step 2: acc (borrows gen form)
Step 1: neut sg, Step 2: gen (нет / без / для)
Step 1: pl, Step 2: prep (в / на / о)
patternRecognition.answer: Step 1: masc sg animate, Step 2: acc (borrows gen form)
patternRecognition.explanation: Учитель is masculine animate. The verb знать takes a direct object in the accusative. For masculine animate the acc adjective borrows the genitive form -ого: старого. The same form would mark a true genitive (нет старого учителя), but the trigger here is знать, not нет.

patternRecognition.question: Why does the adjective end in -ой?
options: Step 1: masc sg, Step 2: instr (с / под / за / над)
Step 1: fem sg, Step 2: prep (в + location)
Step 1: neut sg, Step 2: gen (нет / для)
patternRecognition.answer: Step 1: fem sg, Step 2: prep (в + location)
patternRecognition.explanation: Школа is feminine. В + location triggers the prepositional. The feminine prep ending is -ой: маленькой. The same -ой also marks the feminine gen, dat, and instr, but the trigger 'в школе' fixes the case as prepositional.

patternRecognition.question: Why does the adjective end in -их?
options: Step 1: pl, Step 2: gen (нет), Step 3: husher rule
Step 1: pl, Step 2: dat (помогать), Step 3: velar rule
Step 1: masc sg, Step 2: instr (с + accompaniment)
Step 1: fem sg, Step 2: prep (в + location)
patternRecognition.answer: Step 1: pl, Step 2: gen (нет), Step 3: husher rule
patternRecognition.explanation: Друзья is plural. 'Нет + gen' triggers the genitive. Plural gen is -ых, but the husher -ш- in хорош- triggers Rule 1: -ых → -их. So хороших. Pair with новых (no rule, hard stem) and русских (velar rule, same surface form -их).

patternRecognition.question: Why does the adjective end in -ому?
options: Step 1: masc sg, Step 2: dat (к + person)
Step 1: masc sg animate, Step 2: acc (animate borrows gen)
Step 1: neut sg, Step 2: gen (нет / для)
patternRecognition.answer: Step 1: masc sg, Step 2: dat (к + person)
patternRecognition.explanation: Друг is masculine. К + person triggers the dative. Masc dat ending is -ому: старому. Compare: я знаю старого друга (acc animate, borrows gen) vs я иду к старому другу (dat). Same stem, different triggers, different endings.

reviewVocab.definition: declension (the change of an adjective's ending across all six cases × two numbers)
reviewVocab.example: В таблице склонения прилагательного 'новый' двенадцать различных форм покрывают все падежи и числа.

reviewVocab.definition: agreement (the rule that an adjective takes endings matching its noun's gender, number, and case)
reviewVocab.example: В фразе 'старого друга' видно согласование: и прилагательное, и существительное стоят в винительном падеже одушевлённого мужского рода.

reviewVocab.definition: orthography, spelling (the husher / velar rule lives here: after к / г / х / ж / ш / ч / щ, write -и not -ы)
reviewVocab.example: В слове 'хороших' видна орфография: основа кончается на шипящий -ш-, поэтому окончание -их, а не -ых.
